title: Non-specific (Mechanical) Neck Pain
qa: Why is non-specific not a "failed" diagnosis? It honestly states that no single structure can be identified and focuses on treatable impairments.
Why treat the thoracic spine for neck pain? Thoracic manipulation can reduce neck pain in the short term and improve range.
What would make you stop cervical mobilisation? Spreading arm symptoms, dizziness or any neurological symptom.
Which outcome measures would you record? NDI, NPRS, rotation range, PSFS.
What is the key ergonomic message? Frequent posture variation is more important than one "perfect" posture.

fields.What a finding means: If arm symptoms are reproduced, use the radiculopathy pathway

fields.How: Prone, thumbs over the spinous or articular process, gentle oscillating pressure
fields.What a finding means: Comparable pain and stiffness at a level guides mobilisation

fields.How: Supine, chin tucked, head lifted about 2.5 cm; time until the chin pokes or head drops
fields.What a finding means: Low endurance is a training target [Ref – to verify norms]

redFlags.Finding: Fever, night sweats, recent infection, IV drug use
Cancer history, unexplained weight loss, constant night pain
Neck pain with chest pain, sweating, breathlessness
Sudden severe "worst ever" headache with neck stiffness

manual.name: Thoracic thrust manipulation
manual.why: Short-term pain relief and improved range [Ref – to verify]
manual.finding: Neck pain with mobility deficit, thoracic stiffness, no contraindication
manual.application: Supine or sitting, high-velocity small-amplitude thrust after consent

manual.name: Cervical mobilisation (unilateral PA, rotation)
manual.application: Grade III to IV oscillations, 3 sets of 30 to 60 s
manual.stop: Symptoms spread to the arm or head

manual.name: Mulligan SNAGs
manual.finding: Movement limited and painful in one direction
manual.application: Sitting, glide along facet plane, patient moves actively

manualNotes: Preferred starting choice: combine manual therapy with exercise. Manual therapy alone is less effective than combined care [Ref – to verify].

exercise.Exercise: Prone or band rows, scapular retraction
Shoulder shrugs and upper trapezius strengthening
Thoracic extension over a towel roll

exerciseNotes: Ergonomic advice: vary posture often; screen at eye level; regular movement breaks. The best posture is the next posture.

modalities.name: Traction
modalities.indicated: Not routine for non-radiating neck pain
modalities.comment: More relevant to radiculopathy [Ref – to verify]

pathway: Visit 1: screen flags, educate (good prognosis, stay active), start range exercises, consider manual therapy.
Weeks 2 to 6: strengthen deep flexors, scapular and upper back muscles; progress load.
Weeks 6 onward: endurance, work and sport demands, self-management plan for recurrences.
